claim: Tensor parallelism is the worst topology on a PCIe fabric without NVLink: it performs 2 all-reduces per layer (86 collectives per forward on 43 layers), and measured PP beats TP by 6.6x on prefill and ~2-3x on aggregate throughput.
note: Four independent measurements on this hardware class plus two independent primary derivations of the collective count.

claim: FSDP/ZeRO-3 moves 3-Psi bytes per step against DDP's 2-Psi, i.e. 1.5x communication volume, not 2x.
note: Two independent primaries derive the same 3-Psi/2-Psi ratio; the blog restates it.

claim: Mixed-precision Adam costs 16 bytes per trainable parameter: 2 (bf16 weight) + 2 (bf16 grad) + 12 (fp32 master + two fp32 moments). Frozen parameters cost only their bf16 weight.
note: The ICLR-2018 mixed-precision paper is the origin; ZeRO, AMSP and the measured TDS run reproduce it.

claim: PWRBRK# on PCIe edge pin B30 silently caps a CMP 170HX at ~88 W / 39.3 TFLOPS, is detected with `nvidia-smi -q | grep -A1 "HW Power Brake Slowdown"`, and is fixed by masking B30 or using a riser that does not route it.
note: The 155.7-vs-39.3 TFLOPS pair is the direct measurement; the other three document the mechanism and detection.

claim: DDP performs one gradient all-reduce per optimizer step, and gradient accumulation requires `model.no_sync()` on all but the final micro-step or DDP all-reduces on every micro-step.
note: PyTorch source plus maintainer confirmation plus the Megatron implementation.

claim: Gradient compression pays off more on slow fabrics, not less: measured gains are larger at 10 Gbps than at 200 Gbps, and coded approximate all-reduce wins on PCIe while losing on NVLink.
note: Four independent compression papers converge on the same fabric-dependence.

claim: When P2P is unavailable, NCCL stages collectives through host shared memory rather than GPU-to-GPU; this is why PCIe-only all-reduce bandwidth collapses.
note: NCCL docs state it directly; the club measures the resulting 6.21-6.30 GB/s host-staged copy rate; TCCL documents the bounce-buffer placement effect.

claim: The CMP 170HX is GA100 (sm_80) with 64 GB HBM2e after unlock, ~1.49-1.6 TB/s HBM bandwidth, 250 W stock cap, no NVLink, no ECC, and no FP8 tensor cores.
note: Five independent hardware references agree on the spec sheet.

claim: Dataset sizes: FineWeb-Edu is 1.3T tokens; FineMath-4+ is 9.6B tokens; Stack-Edu is ~125B tokens across 15 languages.
note: Each dataset card is primary for its own size; SmolLM2 and the FineWeb paper corroborate.

claim: Sparse attention's advantage is context-length-dependent with a crossover well above 32k: token-granular selection loses at 32k, block-granular wins, and the published KV-cache wins are decode-side numbers.
note: Six independent sparse-attention papers converge on the length-dependence, though they disagree on the exact crossover.

claim: A 1M-token global batch is far below the measured critical batch size late in training (~16.8M tokens on OLMo 1B/7B), but CBS is near zero at initialization, so batch-size warmup is required.
note: Merrill et al. measure the plateau; McCandlish et al. originate the noise-scale model; Goyal et al. establish the warmup requirement.
